cohort: The study included 1,288 Chinese primiparous and multiparous pregnant women in late pregnancy.
finding: Fear of childbirth (FOC) was positively associated with a preference for cesarean section, but neither FOC nor this preference significantly increased actual cesarean section rates.
mod_finding: Fear of childbirth increased the likelihood of preferring a cesarean section, but did not significantly impact the actual delivery mode; however, childbirth education was associated with higher rates of vaginal delivery.
